gaps.quote: where $\mu$ is the number of central wires in one invocation
gaps.note: False. In the paper (line 656) m = h^3 = 1000000 is the matrix dimension, i.e. the number of address fields per chunk (line 1089-1093: H, D are vectors of m fields). The number of central wires per invocation is c_b = 100 (line 775), and the central wires are not what sets the matrix size. The bound s < W m and the later 'mu < 2^20' only make sense for m = 10^6.

The page never gives the value of mu (and its stated meaning, central-wire count, would give 100), so the reader cannot check mu < 2^20; it is not marked cited. The paper (lines 656, 1332) uses m = 10^6 < 2^20.

gaps.quote: by a restoration device the paper introduces as new
gaps.note: Misattribution. The paper (lines 708-711) says the cancellation of arbitrary initial scratch values is a linear instance of the restoration construction for transparent computation of Buhrman, Cleve, Koucky, Loff and Speelman, not a device it introduces. Also the paper's lemma (line 729-737) gives (X,Y) -> (-Y,X), which is an exchange only in the bit (F_2) construction.

gaps.quote: The shear is such an invocation, with $D$ as $X$ and $H$ as $Y$, so it is exact for any initial auxiliary contents.
gaps.note: Not what the paper does and not checkable from the page. The lemma about forward invocations concerns scalar banks x_S, y_S; in the paper (lines 1495-1535) the shear H<-H+D on arrays is obtained by assigning frames Phi_M to each role stream and edge, applying Phi_{A_e} on each edge, with the endpoint identity M_out(rho(w)) - M_in(w) = I_m on every role. The page never says how a bank invocation turns into an address shear on arrays.

gaps.term: missing hypotheses of the width bound
gaps.quote: At depth $d$, the $s$ smaller calls are interchanges of width $\mu^{d-1}$ on streams of volume $V/W$
gaps.note: The paper's Proposition (line 1475-1490) needs fields over a fixed prime radix q, widths that are powers m^k of m measured in radix-q digits, and a row field before both chunks of length divisible by W^k so that the row split into W streams can be repeated d times. The page omits all of these, mixes width in bits (u) with width in digits (mu^d), and never explains how arbitrary u is reached from powers of mu (paper Lemma, lines 1631-1740: padding rows and base-m decomposition), so the claimed O(V u^tau) for arbitrary u does not follow from the recursion shown.
